messages:
alice: Heads-up — seeing a big p95 spike on /rerank from 03:14-03:27 UTC for customer Searchly. 504s and 502s, gateway timeouts. :rotating_light: metric: rerank.p95 went from ~1.9s -> 10.8s, error rate from 0.3% -> 6%.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout at 03:05 complete on v2.3.1 (no errors reported during canary).
ben: Do we have a sample request + gateway trace? suspect huge candidate lists or backpressure.
alice: Pasted a cleaned repro payload and a gateway log snippet below. note candidate_count ~120000 in some requests.
```
POST /v1/rerank HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "query": "best restaurants",
  "candidates": [ ... large array ... ],
  "candidate_count": 120000
}
```
```
[2026-03-15T03:16:42Z] gateway: upstream timeout -> 504 (rerank-service) trace_id=tr_0xabc
[2026-03-15T03:16:42Z] gateway: retrying (attempt=1)
[2026-03-15T03:16:42Z] gateway: upstream 502 (rerank-core) trace_id=tr_0xabd
```
carla: That's a classic fanout/backpressure. Huge candidate lists blow up batching and KV cache lookups. Retries from gateway only amplify. Are these coming from a single Searchly job or many customers?
diego: Confirmed — top origin IPs are three large Searchly workers hitting same route, QPS spike ~80. Their job iterates candidate lists of variable length; some batches 50-150k.
support-oncall: Searchly is reporting customer impact and billing confusion — they saw inflated tokens because of retries. They want a fast mitigation + possible credit for excess.
diego: Short-term mitigations we can apply now:
- per-customer QPS cap (apply route-level rate-limit to Searchly client_id)
- disable gateway automatic retries for /rerank or lower retry attempts
- enforce candidate_count cap at the gateway and return 413 with helpful message
- fallback to smaller model variant to reduce per-request compute
Example: `curl -X PATCH https://api.redwood.internal/config/rate-limits -d '{"client_id":"searchly","qps":50}'`
ben: Can we do an immediate config change? if we throttle them, will it queue and delay their jobs or return 429?
diego: We'll set it to 50 QPS with 429 on excess (no retries). Implemented at 03:33 UTC. Also toggled gatewayRetries.maxAttempts to 1 for /rerank.
alice: After the QPS cap + retries change, p95 dropped to ~1.9s and error rate back to ~0.6% within 3m. customer reports fewer 504s. quick numbers: before 03:33 p95 10.8s, 504s/min 18 -> after 03:36 p95 1.9s, 504s/min 1.
ben: Nice. Need repro for ENG-REPRO. Diego can you paste the script to reproduce locally?
diego: Repro steps: run this against staging rerank with gatewayRetries enabled, high concurrency.
```
# repro.sh
for i in {1..200}; do
  curl -s -X POST https://staging.api/rerank -d '{"query":"x","candidates_count":100000, "candidates":[...]} &' 
done
wait
```
This triggers queueing and KV thrash. Also repro with `candidate_count` 30k at QPS 60 to see p95 uplift.
carla: Long term: add server-side candidate_count hard limit (configurable per-tenant), surface throttling headers and an SDK error to help integrators. Also add a rerank circuit-breaker metric so console can auto-alert before 5xx ramp.
support-oncall: I'll file a CS ticket for Searchly credits and summarize what we did. Need a short bullet list for them.
alice: Action items: 1) create ENG ticket to add candidate cap + circuit-breaker (owner: carla) 2) add runbook step for per-tenant QPS caps (owner: ben) 3) CX ticket for credits (owner: support-oncall) 4) postmortem if recurrence within 72h (owner: alice).
carla: ack. I'll start the ENG ticket with logs and the staging repro.
ben: I'll add the runbook entries and a dashboard tile for rerank.circuit_breaker.count.
support-oncall: I'll draft the credit note and send to Searchly PM.
alice: Thanks all — keeping this thread updated with any follow-ups. :thumbsup:
